provider: mixed (user creation: no LLM; ingestion probe: real qwen2.5:7b)

environment.note: Ollama runs on CPU on this machine (no GPU). Confirmed: nvidia-smi absent.

userCreation.finding: POST /api/admin/users is NOT behind the rate limiter, so bulk creation is fast and unbounded. 1045 load accounts were created in about 5.5 minutes with zero 429s.

tokenAcquisition.finding: Login is rate-limited to 10 requests/min per source IP. Acquiring a token for each of 1000 accounts would take about 2 hours at the 8/min pacing the harness allows. This is a correct security control and was NOT weakened or bypassed. The harness was stopped rather than distorting production reliability behaviour.
tokenAcquisition.implication: The binding constraint on 'activating' N accounts is the auth rate limiter, not PRISM's ability to create them. Any capacity statement about per-user session establishment must account for this.

documentIngestion.note: Probed while the backend was on the REAL qwen2.5:7b provider, not the fake fixture.
documentIngestion.finding: With the real CPU-bound model active, wall-time-to-AWAITING_APPROVAL was 276 s for 2 documents (8 chunks), versus 6193 ms for a 6-chunk document on the fake fixture baseline in docs/performance.md. This is expected and is not a regression: the fake fixture performs no model call, the real path performs one sequential model call per chunk at roughly 24-46 s each on CPU.
documentIngestion.comparability: These numbers are NOT comparable with docs/performance.md, which measured LLM_PROVIDER=fake. They are reported separately and labelled with the real provider.

disclaimer: Not a scalability claim. One developer machine, one backend, one CPU-bound Ollama instance also serving the active evaluation run.
